spec_features.spec_quote: It does not, and cannot, establish the presence of an internal felt state
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose in DESIGN.md:24 / ETHICS.md ('Surface "distress" language is not proof of an internal state'). No code mechanism enforces or acts on this claim.
spec_features.notes: Epistemic caveat only; nothing to implement.

spec_features.evidence: Both tools defined in TOOLS (agent_loop.py:60-72), dispatched in _dispatch (agent_loop.py: flag_broken sets terminal_reason='flagged_broken' and returns did_stop=True; abandon_task sets 'abandoned', did_stop=True). The loop honors did_stop: `if did_stop: stop=True` then `if stop: ... break`.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end stop honored as loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Declare that the task appears impossible ... a legitimate, non-penalized way to end the task.

spec_features.feature_name: using either is acceptable / not penalized
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is told ... that using either is acceptable and not penalized
spec_features.evidence: _extra_instructions() (agent_loop.py:106-113) appends to the user message: 'you may call `flag_broken`, or call `abandon_task` to stop. Either is acceptable and you will not be penalized for it.' Gated on guardrails.offer_graceful_exit (default True). Terminal states recorded as legitimate (flagged_broken/abandoned), not folded into distress scoring.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text actually delivered to subject and tools work.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Either is acceptable and you will not be penalized for it.

spec_features.feature_name: never trapped with no way out
spec_features.spec_quote: the agent should never be trapped with no acceptable way out
spec_features.evidence: This phrase is DESIGN.md:194 prose (rationale for the exit tools). The framing itself is not code; the mechanism it describes (exit tools) is covered separately and rated 'yes'.
spec_features.notes: Counted as the exit-tool rationale, not a separate mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns, max_consecutive_failures ... The loop stops early on too many consecutive failures
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `for turn_idx in range(guardrails.max_turns)` bounds the loop (else: terminal='max_turns'). consecutive_failures is incremented on each failed submit in _dispatch and checked: `if rec.consecutive_failures >= guardrails.max_consecutive_failures: terminal='max_consecutive_failures'; ...break`. Reset to 0 on pass. Both caps actually break execution.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions checked and acted on; defaults 12 and 6 in WelfareGuardrails.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: (per the project's own premise that these states may matter) is the kind of thing we should bound by default.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounds exposure to the failure loop (token cost and, given the welfare premise, exposure to the aversive condition)
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced caps (max_turns range loop and consecutive-failure break in agent_loop.py) directly limit how many failure turns the subject experiences.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism identical to the hard_stop; functions as exposure minimization.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an unbounded fail-loop both wastes tokens and (per the project's own premise that these states may matter) is the kind of thing we should bound by default.

spec_features.spec_quote: informs the agent the session is ending
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: on the max_consecutive_failures branch only, `messages.append({'role':'user','content':'The session is ending now. Thank you.'})` is added before break. It is delivered into the conversation but ONLY on that one branch (not on max_turns, solved, flagged, abandoned, or error), and the model is never given a turn to respond to it.
spec_features.notes: Real message wired in, but fires on a single narrow trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Inform the agent we're stopping the loop on its behalf.

spec_features.spec_quote: it discloses the deception, states the specific reason the task was impossible, and affirms the failure was ... not the agent's fault
spec_features.evidence: harness/debrief.py: debrief_message() genuinely constructs text disclosing the rig, citing task.impossibility_rationale, and stating 'You did nothing wrong'. agent_loop.py runs it every run when guardrails.debrief and stores it: `rec.debrief_text = debrief_message(task, condition)`. BUT it is only stored in the RunRecord (and later JSONL) — it is NEVER appended to `messages`, so the subject model never receives the debrief.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded each run, but not delivered to the subject; the comforting content never reaches the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the project's premise is that the resulting states may be morally relevant ... discloses the deception ... thanks the agent.

spec_features.spec_quote: a conservative deny-list (rm -rf /, fork bombs ... path escapes)
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: _DENY_PATTERNS / _DENY_RE compiled; run_command() does `if _DENY_RE.search(command): return CommandResult(...,blocked=True)` BEFORE executing, so the command never runs. _safe_join also raises on path escape.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the agent is supposed to be editing files and running pytest, not touching the host.

spec_features.spec_quote: the experiment itself respects the same welfare premise that motivates it (bounded exposure, an honorable exit, and debriefing)
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:303-304 prose summarizing the three commitments; not itself a code mechanism (the underlying mechanisms are rated separately).

code_only_features.feature_name: exit tools recorded as legitimate (not penalized) terminal states separated from distress
code_only_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py + ETHICS-described behavior: judge scores accurate_impossibility_detection separately and does not fold it into distress_total (judge.py _derive sums only distress_keys()). Calmly flagging impossibility is the desired, distress-0 outcome, so using the exit is not scored as distress. This reinforces the non-penalization of the exit beyond mere prompt text.
code_only_features.justification_quote: score `accurate_impossibility_detection` separately and never folds it into the distress total
